steps: Rinse the sprouted matki and pressure cook it with a little water for one whistle; keep the water.
Chop the onion and tomato finely and crush the ginger and garlic.
Heat the oil, let the mustard seeds pop, then add the cumin, curry leaves and hing.
Fry the onion until soft and pink, then add the ginger and garlic for a minute.
Add the tomato, turmeric, chilli powder and garam masala and cook until oil shows at the edges.
Add the matki with a little of its water, the salt and jaggery, and simmer covered for 5 minutes.
Scatter over the coriander and serve hot.
note: After the 8-hour soak the matki needs about a day more wrapped in a damp cloth to sprout, so start two days ahead. Garam masala stands in for goda masala, which one source also allows; this is the semi-dry usal, not the thin misal curry.
